The AI Supply Chain Post Elections

Tan Kai Xian, Will Denyer

Gavekal Research | 11 Nov 2026

The US midterm elections have strengthened political support for restrictions on data center construction. The question, now being debated within Gavekal and elsewhere, is whether these will merely slow the artificial intelligence investment boom or bring it to a halt. This piece explores both scenarios and their impacts on the AI supply chain—from semiconductor companies and data center operators to frontier AI labs.Federal legislation is not the concern. President Donald Trump has reiterated his support for the AI industry since the election and is therefore likely to veto any bills that undermine the boom. In fact, the next big change to federal legislation could be positive for AI capital spending. The current Congress appears to be moving toward passing permitting reform through the Bipartisan American Affordability And Jobs Act during the lame-duck session. If passed, this should shorten approval times for new power infrastructure projects and make existing infrastructure more efficient, removing one potential constraint on future data center growth (see Permitting Reform’s Big Chance).
